newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom launches cut-price IDD.
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom launches cut-price IDD.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Wednesday it was launching two cut-price international direct dial (IDD) services.
"It's not a big change of strategy -- it's another component of the customer retention strategy," said Jeremy Godfrey, Hongkong Telecom's director of marketing.
The utility has a theoretical monopoly on IDD calls to and from Hong Kong, but has been losing business to call-back operators offering hefty discounts.

It said its new "IDD 001 Savings Plan 1" offered discounts of up to 10 percent on some of the most popular call routes, while an "0060 International Call Service" would cover 12 popular call destinations during the initial launch period.

The 0060 International Call Service offered three alternative rates -- a standard rate, a volume rate for monthly spending of more than HK$3,000, and a promotion rate applying to off-peak hours and weekends.

For example, while the prevailing IDD rate for calls to the U.S. was HK$6.80 a minute, Hongkong Telecom's 0060 standard rate would be HK$2.98 a minute, falling to HK$2.68 for the volume rate and HK$1.99 for off-peak calls.
Godfrey said the company offered the 0060 service because there was clearly a large segment of the marketplace seeking an affordable if slightly lower-quality international service.
The discounts come at a time when rival services are wooing Hongkong Telecom subscribers -- the company said in November that it had lost 15 percent of its IDD market share.
"It's not too little, too late. It's a response to evolving market conditions," said Bear Stearns' Daniel Widdicombe.
"It's probably quite a pragmatic response because there's an inexorable trend towards lower IDD prices."
But Widdicombe said the fact remained that Hongkong Telecom was in a saturated market and its IDD monopoly was under siege.
"They're being hit," he said. "Their crown jewels are being attacked by global trends towards much lower IDD prices."
Salomon Brothers analyst Dan Sherman said the price cuts might help stem the loss of customers.
"It's been shown that if the prices are within, say 10 percent to 15 percent (of cut-price operators), the customers don't switch -- it's just not worth the hassle," Sherman said.
Hongkong Telecom shares ended HK$0.10 firmer at HK$13.65.
